scenario: AITA for keeping my son during my visitation instead of giving in to his mother? | I guess some backstory is due here. My ex and I have an 8 year old son, and we have been split up for a few years now. I have every other weekend parenting time along with a day during the week. It’s not enough time for me, but it’s what was legally decided through court. Her and I do not have the best relationship currently because I feel like I’m always being taken advantage of and I allow it because she always uses the “it’s for your son” excuse. I cherish my time with my son, but for the longest time, I allowed my ex to alter the parenting schedule to suit my son’s needs, whether for activities or family or if he just wasn’t feeling well. I always tried to be as accommodating as possible, even if it meant I didn’t see him for a week or more. Anyway, last Wednesday I was supposed to get him overnight, his mother called me and I asked if he could stay there since his cousin from out of town was staying with them. I reluctantly agreed but told her I wanted to get him Thursday instead. She agreed, and when Thursday came around, I texted her after work and said I was on my way to get him. She said they weren’t home, and I had to press her for information why. She decided to take the kids to a lake and said I needed to stop being grumpy because my son was having fun. We argued back and forth and since I did not drive all the way out to the lake to get him when I shouldn’t have had to in the first place, I told her that we should switch weekends (last weekend was hers, this one is mine) so that I had my make up time and his activities with her that fell on my weekend wouldn’t be interrupted. She refused, so now that my weekend is coming up, I’m not getting him at my regular time today because he’s at an amusement park with her family, and I am expected to give up even more of my valuable time tomorrow for their annual 4th of July party. Am I the asshole for putting my foot down and keeping my son during their family function so that I can enjoy time my son during my scheduled time?

prediction.raw: In this situation, it is important to balance the legal custody arrangement with the well-being of your son and the dynamics of your relationship with your ex. Here is a structured approach to address the issue: 1. **Legal Custody**: The custody arrangement is legally binding, and you have the right to spend time with your son as per the court's decision. It is reasonable to assert this right to ensure consistency and stability for your son. 2. **Communication**: Open and respectful communication with your ex is crucial. Clearly express the importance of sticking to the schedule and how deviations affect both you and your son. This can help prevent future conflicts and ensure mutual understanding. 3. **Flexibility and Compromise**: While it is important to maintain the schedule, occasional flexibility can be beneficial. However, this should be a mutual effort and not one-sided. If your ex is unwilling to compromise, it may be necessary to revisit the custody arrangement. 4. **Impact on Your Son**: Consider the emotional well-being of your son. Consistent time with both parents is important, but so is participating in family activities. Strive to find a balance that respects both aspects. 5. **Addressing Manipulation**: If your ex is manipulating the situation, it may be necessary to seek mediation or legal advice to address these issues. It is important to protect your rights and ensure a fair arrangement for your son. In conclusion, asserting your right to spend time with your son as per the legal schedule is not being an asshole. It is a reasonable approach to ensure consistency and fairness. However, maintaining open communication and striving for mutual compromise can help create a healthier environment for everyone involved.

Honestly, it's not enough time for me, but it's what the court decided, so I have to work with it. My ex and I don't have the best relationship right now. I feel like I'm always being taken advantage of, and I let it happen because she always uses the "it's for the son" excuse. I really cherish the time I get to spend with my son, but for a long time, I let my ex change the parenting schedule to suit my son's needs, whether it was for activities, family stuff, or if he just wasn't feeling well. I tried to be as accommodating as possible, even if it meant I didn't see him for a week or more. Last Wednesday, I was supposed to get him overnight. My ex called me and asked if he could stay with her because her cousin from out of town was visiting. I reluctantly agreed but told her I wanted to get him on Thursday instead. She agreed, and when Thursday came around, I texted her after work to say I was on my way to get him. She said they weren't home and I had to press her for information why. She decided to take the kid to a lake and said I needed to stop being grumpy because my son was having fun.
